test_title: SSC Stenographer 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 10 Dec, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Nipped in the bud

options.text: Very promising at a young age
To stop something immediately so that it does not become a worse problem

solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 4**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"nipped in the bud"** means to stop something immediately so that it does not become a worse problem. (समस्या बढ़ने से पहले उसे रोक लेना)

 
 
• **Example:** The company nipped the potential scandal in the bud by addressing the issue promptly.
 
 
 
• **To stop something immediately** refers to taking quick action to prevent a problem from escalating. (तुरंत रोकना)
 
 
• **Example:** He nipped the argument in the bud by changing the topic.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 4**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **To remove unnecessary items** (अनावश्यक वस्तुओं को हटाना):

 
 
• **Example:** She decided to remove unnecessary items from her closet to make more space.
 
 
 
• **To cut the bud** (कली को काटना):
 
 
• **Example:** The gardener cut the bud to encourage the plant to grow more flowers.
 
 
 
• **Very promising at a young age** (किसी के लिए बहुत आशाजनक होना):
 
 
• **Example:** The young athlete was very promising at a young age and showed great potential.
 
 

164:Tf8a,
The correct answer is **Option 2**.
